title: Take K of Each Character From Left and Right
summary: Given a string s made up of 'a', 'b', and 'c', and a non-negative integer k, you can remove characters from either end of the string.
statement: Given a string s made up of 'a', 'b', and 'c', and a non-negative integer k, you can remove characters from either end of the string. Determine the least time required to remove at least k of each character, or return -1 if it's impossible.
constraints: The string contains only a, b, and c and has length at least one.
One move removes the current leftmost or rightmost character.
Return the fewest moves collecting at least k of every character, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Taking a prefix and suffix is equivalent to leaving one contiguous middle substring.
Count all letters, then grow a middle window while at least k of each remain outside it.
Move the left boundary whenever adding the right character would leave too few copies outside.
The longest valid middle minimizes the complementary prefix-plus-suffix length; insufficient totals make the task impossible.
editorial: The longest valid middle minimizes the complementary prefix-plus-suffix length; insufficient totals make the task impossible.

tests.explanation: Keeping the longest valid middle leaves eight characters to take from the ends.
No b or c exists, so collecting one of each is impossible.
